concerns.text: The specification requires computing 3‑D geometry descriptors and training a “Full Model” baseline (FR‑004, FR‑005). The original idea only calls for a lightweight regression model using SMILES‑derived features; 3‑D descriptors were never requested, constituting unnecessary scope expansion.

A sensitivity analysis that sweeps high‑packing thresholds and applies a Bonferroni correction (FR‑007, FR‑008) is introduced, but the idea does not mention any threshold‑sweep or multiple‑testing correction. This adds work beyond the stated research question.
Variance‑inflation‑factor diagnostics on all predictor variables (FR‑009) are required, yet the idea never calls for multicollinearity checks. This is an unrequested analysis.
A power analysis based on bootstrapping (FR‑019) is specified, but the original methodology only required a permutation test for significance. Power analysis was not part of the idea’s scope.
Streaming inference with batch size ≤ 50 to avoid OOM errors (FR‑020) is mandated, although the idea assumes a “lightweight” CPU‑only pipeline without such memory‑management constraints.
The spec adds explicit generation of “atom‑type count features” (FR‑021) which were not mentioned in the idea’s description of feature extraction.
Feature ablation comparing Primary and Full models (FR‑013) is required, yet the idea never requested a comparative ablation study.

Success Criterion SC‑002 demands a Bonferroni‑corrected permutation‑test p‑value ≤ 0.05 and a minimum Spearman ρ ≥ 0.3. The original idea only required reporting correlation and a permutation test; imposing a specific corrected p‑value threshold is beyond the original scope.
SC‑003 introduces a conditional null‑result check (ρ < 0.2 ⇒ p ≥ 0.05) that was not part of the idea’s evaluation plan.
Robustness across three high‑packing thresholds (SC‑004) is a new requirement not present in the idea.
The end‑to‑end runtime limit of ≤ 6 hours on a free‑tier GitHub Actions runner (SC‑005) is an engineering constraint absent from the original idea.
Logging a deviation when the permutation test exceeds a 4‑hour timeout (SC‑006) adds a failure‑handling requirement not specified in the idea.

The specification subtly redefines the research question from a single inquiry—“How does SMILES‑encoded topology relate to packing efficiency?”—to a multi‑part investigation focusing on statistical significance thresholds, robustness to arbitrary cut‑offs, and contribution of 3‑D descriptors. This drift changes the scientific focus and may dilute the original hypothesis.
